# ODUTQA-MDC: A Task for Open-Domain Underspecified Tabular QA with Multi-turn Dialogue-based Clarification

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#odutqa-mdc)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.499.pdf) · ACL 2026 long-paper proceedings, pp. 10907–10928

**Reading coverage:** All 22 pages, main sections 1–6 and Limitations; Appendices A–D with construction, paraphrase audit, simulator mechanics, statistics, supplementary/ablation experiments, algorithms and all displayed prompts.

## Research question

Queries may omit their intended attribute, table scope or entity condition, making open-corpus table retrieval and SQL generation fail before conventional parsing can succeed.

## Method

ODUTQA-MDC perturbs RETQA templates and entity values to create single and mixed SELECT/FROM/WHERE underspecification. A simulator reveals dictionary-held corrections only after the system predicts the required detection label. MAIC-TQA combines a fine-tuned intent/slot model, scope validation, table retrieval and SQL execution with bounded clarification loops.

## Evaluation

The Chinese real-estate collection contains 209 tables and 25,105 QA pairs with a 6:2:2 split. Five LLM backbones compare clarification-enabled MAIC-TQA against clarification-free SLUTQA. Measures separate detection, table retrieval, SQL executability and exact execution-result match; ablations remove each clarification stage.

## What the results support

Clarification improves retrieval and execution accuracy in the reported setup. For Qwen3 32B, fixed clarification raises execution accuracy from 24.20% to 57.44%; dynamic paraphrasing changes outcomes differently across models. Scope and condition clarification account for the largest ablation losses.

## Limits and qualifications

The task is deliberately filtered toward recoverable, answerable targets and excludes complex aggregation and broad linguistic ambiguity. Its simulator rewards exact label detection with privileged target information; natural paraphrasing does not test human goal changes or refusal. MAIC’s BERT is fine-tuned on the new dataset while baseline BERT is loaded from its original release. Cross-domain generalization is proposed, not demonstrated.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A useful benchmark for coupling missing-information detection with table retrieval and clarification, provided its controlled correction protocol is distinguished from general answerability assessment.

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.
